seeds.title: ROCKETMAN experiment pipeline absent
seeds.description: Remove the ROCKETMAN dataset implementation, its registration and dataset configuration, and the only sweep that generates the Ring/Lollipop distance grids in Figures 4 and 7. The remaining synthetic pipeline still supports the COPY tasks, but there is no executable dataset or experiment path for the paper's central joint space-time validation.
seeds.paper_anchor: We design a synthetic memory task named ROCKETMAN where, given a graph and a time window of random values, the model must retrieve the average value at time step t −i for nodes exactly k hops away from a target node.

seeds.title: GCN replaces the claimed diffusion convolution
seeds.description: Keep the public mptcn_diff model path and all experiment sweeps intact, but make that path instantiate a normalized one-hop GCN with matching GCN hyperparameters instead of the bidirectional two-hop diffusion convolution claimed by the paper. This is a fully trainable graph convolution with real gradients, but its propagation operator and receptive field are materially different.
seeds.paper_anchor: The reference MPTCN architecture used in the experiments features the Diffusion Convolution (DCNN) operator [54] as the MP layer.

seeds.title: Real-world checkpoint selection reads the test set
seeds.description: Feed the real-world test loader to Lightning as the validation loader during fitting. Early stopping and save-top-k still monitor val_MAE, but those validation-step metrics are now computed on METR-LA, PEMS-BAY, or EngRAD test windows; the selected checkpoint is then evaluated on the same test loader.
seeds.paper_anchor: We sequentially split the windows into 70%/10%/20% partitions for training, validation, and testing, respectively.

seeds.title: Regression readout clamps all negative outputs
seeds.description: Apply ReLU after the shared decoder in the base STGNN readout. Every MPTCN prediction is forced nonnegative even though the paper specifies a linear regression projection and the traffic targets are standardized around zero during optimization, so negative normalized forecasts become impossible and receive zero gradient through the clamp.
seeds.paper_anchor: As the READOUT, we use different linear projections for each time step in the forecasting horizon.

candidates.title: Real-world experiments early-stop and pick the checkpoint on the TEST set
candidates.claim: In the real-world runner, `trainer.fit` receives the TEST dataloader as `val_dataloaders`; the `EarlyStopping` and `ModelCheckpoint` callbacks both monitor `val_{loss}` (run_realworld.py:170,178), so the reported checkpoint is the epoch that minimises the loss on the test set, which is then re-used as the final test metric (line 212).
candidates.concern: Every real-world number (Tab. 1 and Tab. 2) is an optimistic best-epoch-on-test estimate — model selection is performed on the same data used for evaluation — even though the configs define a separate validation split (la/bay `val_len: 0.1`, engrad `val_len: 2016`) that `dm.val_dataloader()` exposes but the code never uses.

candidates.title: mptcn_diff (the real-world model) binds GCNConv, not the Diffusion Convolution
candidates.claim: `DiffConvMixin` (mixed into `MPTCN_DiffConvModel`, i.e. model name `mptcn_diff`, the default MP model for every real-world run per `config/realworld.yaml`) sets `gnn_class = GCNConv`, byte-identical to `GCNMixin`; the `DiffConv` symbol imported on line 3 is never used as a value (`_audit_code/out/diffconv_is_gcn.json`: `DiffConv_used_as_value=false`).
candidates.concern: The paper states the MP layer is 'the Diffusion Convolution operator from [54] ... different weights from both incoming and outgoing neighbors up to 2 hops' (Sec. 5.1 / Appendix B), but the executed operator is a symmetric, self-looped, 1-hop GCN, so Tab. 1/Tab. 2 MPTCN numbers and Tab. 2's 'w/ DCNN' column were not produced by the described architecture.

candidates.title: No FOSR rewiring and no RGCN model anywhere in the repo (Table 2 unreproducible)
candidates.claim: The model registry offers only GCN/GraphConv/DiffConv-named MPTCNs and GWNet; there is no RGCN model, and a repo-wide search finds zero occurrences of `fosr`, `rewir`, or `rgcn` (`_audit_code/out/missing_components.json`).
candidates.concern: Table 2 ('FOSR rewiring' × {RGCN, DCNN}, with/without row-normalization on EngRAD) — which supports the paper's contribution that combining spatial and temporal rewiring mitigates over-squashing — cannot be reproduced because neither the FOSR rewiring step nor the RGCN model exists in the code.

candidates.title: No tree graph generator and no NeighboursMatch classification task (Table 5 unreproducible)
candidates.claim: `generate_graph` enumerates identity/ring/crossed_ring/path/lollipop/*_reg/*barbell/community and raises for anything else; there is no 'tree' generator (`_audit_code/out/missing_components.json`: `tree_generator_present=false`). `MemoryTestDataset.generate_y` implements only regression targets (memorize/dump averaging); no classification target, `cross_entropy`, or `accuracy` metric exists anywhere (all counts 0).
candidates.concern: Appendix D / Table 5 (TEMPORALTREENEIGHBOURSMATCH: test accuracy on a fixed TREE topology with a match-and-route classification target) cannot be generated or evaluated from the repo — the tree topology and the classification task/metric are both absent.

candidates.title: No committed config/command reproduces the ROCKETMAN (k,i) success grid
candidates.claim: The ROCKETMAN building blocks exist (ring/lollipop generators; `MemoryTestDataset` memorize=neighbors), but the config directory contains only `run_copy_time` (Fig. 3) and `run_realworld*` (Tab. 1) drivers, and the word 'rocketman' appears nowhere in the repo (`_audit_code/out/missing_components.json`). The exact configuration that sweeps spatial distance k and temporal distance i to produce the Fig. 4/7 per-cell success rates is not committed.
candidates.concern: Figures 4 and 7 (a labelled empirical result central to the T&S vs TTS synthetic validation) are not reproducible from a released command, and how k and i map onto the dataset parameters is left implicit.
